rows.official_guidance: Non-EEA nationals cannot legally start work in Norway without a residence permit for skilled workers. UDI processing typically takes 8–16 weeks — this is the single longest lead-time item in the whole move.
rows.action_required: Apply for Norwegian work permit / residence permit for skilled workers via UDI

rows.official_guidance: UDI requires a formal offer/confirmation of employment from the Norwegian employer as part of the skilled-worker application. Prepare and send it early so it never blocks the permit file.
rows.action_required: Provide employer letter of employment confirmation for the UDI application

rows.official_guidance: Confirm the employee’s passport is valid well beyond the move date. Renewals from abroad add weeks — check now, not at the airport.
rows.action_required: Check passport validity

rows.official_guidance: Some roles require Norwegian recognition of foreign qualifications (NOKUT or sector regulator). Confirm whether the role needs it and start the assessment now.
rows.action_required: Educational credential recognition (if applicable)

rows.official_guidance: Norway left EU accession on the table decades ago: it is in the EEA and Schengen, but NOT the EU. French employees (and HR) often assume intra-EU rules apply. Norway still requires a D-number, skattekort, and — for EEA nationals — police registration. None of these are automatic from an EU passport.
rows.action_required: Norway is EEA, not EU — don’t assume EU free-movement rules cover everything

rows.official_guidance: Start the housing search in the destination city. Rental markets in Oslo, Bergen and Stavanger move fast, and a Norwegian address is needed for several registrations later in the timeline.
rows.action_required: Research housing options

rows.official_guidance: Collect the documents the UDI application and onboarding may require: French police clearance (casier judiciaire), medical certificate if the role requires it, and certified translations where needed.
rows.action_required: Gather supporting documents — French police clearance, medical certificate if required

rows.official_guidance: The D-number is the temporary Norwegian ID everything else hangs off: no D-number means no bank account, no skattekort, and no payroll. Book the Skatteetaten appointment now — HR coordinates, the employee attends with passport and employment contract.
rows.action_required: Apply for D-number at the Norwegian Tax Administration (Skatteetaten)

rows.official_guidance: EEA nationals must register their right of residence with the tax office (Skattekontoret) — an EU passport alone is not enough. This step is routinely missed because it has no equivalent in intra-EU moves.
rows.action_required: Register EU/EEA right of residence at Skattekontoret

rows.official_guidance: Norwegian banks require a D-number before opening an account, and payroll cannot be paid to a foreign account long-term. Start as soon as the D-number is issued.
rows.action_required: Open Norwegian bank account

rows.official_guidance: Confirm the employing entity is properly registered in the Brønnøysund Register Centre. Payroll reporting (A-melding) and withholding tax registration both depend on it.
rows.action_required: Verify Norwegian employer Brønnøysund registration is complete

rows.official_guidance: A-melding is Norway’s mandatory monthly employer report of salary, tax deductions and employment to the authorities. It MUST be active before the first paycheck runs — setting it up after the fact is a compliance breach, not a formality.
rows.action_required: Set up A-melding (employer payroll reporting)

rows.official_guidance: The skattekort must be in place BEFORE the first paycheck, not after. Without it the employer is legally required to withhold 50% of salary. Apply via Skatteetaten once the D-number exists — HR coordinates the timing against the payroll calendar.
rows.action_required: Apply for skattekort (tax card)

rows.official_guidance: EEA nationals are legally required to register with the Norwegian police within 3 months of arrival. Appointment slots in Oslo can run out weeks ahead — book now. This is the item HR teams most often assume an EU passport makes unnecessary.
rows.action_required: Police registration for EEA nationals

rows.official_guidance: Register the employment for Norwegian withholding tax so deductions run correctly from the first payroll cycle.
rows.action_required: Withholding tax registration

rows.official_guidance: Verify and document the employee’s right to work in Norway before the start date — permit or registered EEA residence, checked and filed.
rows.action_required: Right-to-work verification

rows.official_guidance: Move-date gate check: payroll cannot run without BOTH the D-number and an active skattekort. Confirm both are in place today, before the first payroll cycle starts.
rows.action_required: Confirm D-number received and skattekort active

rows.official_guidance: Post-arrival check: confirm the police registration appointment actually happened and the confirmation document is on file.
rows.action_required: Confirm police registration completed

rows.official_guidance: Check the first Norwegian payslip: correct skattekort rate applied, no 50% emergency withholding. If deductions are wrong, fix them in the next A-melding cycle immediately.
rows.action_required: Verify first paycheck has correct tax deduction

rows.official_guidance: A Critical Skills permit requires a contract of at least 24 months with the Irish entity directly. Contractor or agency structures do not qualify. Everything below is measured from the day this is signed.
rows.action_required: Signed employment contract (2-year minimum, direct employment)

rows.official_guidance: Filed via Employment Permits Online. This is the EMPLOYER’s application, not the employee’s — HR owns it. Typical processing runs several weeks and nothing downstream can start until it is granted.
rows.action_required: Submit the Critical Skills Employment Permit application to DETE

rows.official_guidance: NON-OBVIOUS: the permit is a labour authorisation from DETE, not immigration permission. It does not by itself allow entry to or residence in Ireland — the entry visa is a separate application to a different authority.
rows.action_required: Employment permit granted by DETE

rows.official_guidance: NON-OBVIOUS: Ireland is outside Schengen, so a Spanish residence card grants no entry right. A visa-required national must hold the ‘D’ visa BEFORE travelling — a mover who has lived in the EU for years will not expect this.
rows.action_required: Apply for the long-stay ‘D’ Employment visa

rows.official_guidance: The entry authorisation itself. Travel booked before this is granted is at risk.
rows.action_required: ‘D’ Employment visa granted (entry authorisation)

rows.official_guidance: NON-OBVIOUS: Ireland is not bound by the EU Long-Term Residents Directive 2003/109/EC, so EU long-term residence or a TIE held in Spain confers no entry or work right in Ireland. The full permit + visa + registration sequence still applies. Ireland is also NOT part of the Schengen Area: a Schengen visa is not valid for travel to Ireland, a national passport or national identity card is required to enter even when arriving from the EEA, and every non-EEA national is subject to Irish immigration control on arrival — permission to enter is granted by an immigration officer at the port of entry and is a separate thing from holding a visa.
rows.actual_reality: ‘Ireland is an EU move, so the documentation is already covered’ is the framing error that generates every other surprise on this corridor, and it fails in three separate directions. IMMIGRATION: the employment permit (DETE), the entry visa (a different authority), permission to enter at the border and IRP registration are four distinct steps, none of which a Spanish TIE does anything for. TAX: the PPSN cannot be applied for from Spain, and Irish emergency-basis PAYE runs until the employment is registered and an RPN issues. ANIMALS: a dog moving Madrid→Dublin still needs Echinococcus multilocularis treatment 24–120 hours before arrival, and TRACES NT certification if it flies unaccompanied — the mover's own words on the verified 2026-08-15 case were “I assumed EU to EU meant the pet paperwork was already done.” Ireland's EU membership is true and is not the point: what governs this corridor is that Ireland opted out of Schengen and of Directive 2003/109/EC, and that its tapeworm-free status is defended by border rules which apply to intra-EU movements too.
rows.action_required: Confirm the employee understands Spanish residence does not transfer, and that Ireland is EU but not Schengen
rows.source_name: Citizens Information — ‘Permission to enter Ireland’: Ireland is not part of the Schengen Area; non-EEA nationals must get permission to enter on arrival and may also need a visa
rows.notes: Corrected 2026-08-17 to close gate rule no_wrong_requirements (wrong item 3, Ireland framed as ‘an EU move’ for documentation purposes) from cvr:ES-IE:2026-08-15:andrea. Secondary sources read 2026-08-17: Department of Foreign Affairs, ‘Visas for Ireland’ (‘A Schengen visa is not valid for travel to Ireland’; all non-EEA nationals are subject to immigration control on arrival), https://ireland.ie/en/dfa/visas-for-ireland/ ; the animal-health leg is sourced on ie:customs:pet-import-dog-eu. Not lawyer-verified.

rows.official_guidance: Only now can the employee travel. Everything above had to complete first — this is the point the free-movement mental model gets wrong.
rows.action_required: Travel to Ireland

rows.official_guidance: Registration with Immigration Service Delivery (Burgh Quay for Dublin) within 90 days of arrival. Appointment slots are the constraint, not the paperwork.
rows.action_required: Register immigration permission — IRP card / Stamp 1

rows.official_guidance: The PPSN is needed before the employment can be registered with Revenue. It is applied for through MyWelfare with a MyGovID account (or by post on form REG1 where the online route is not possible) and it CANNOT be applied for before the mover is in Ireland — Citizens Information states expressly that someone intending to relocate must wait until they are in the country. The application requires proof of identity (a current passport for a non-EU citizen), proof of an Irish address no more than three months old, and proof of why the number is needed. It also includes a MANDATORY in-person appointment at a PPS Number Allocation Centre / Intreo Centre, booked as part of the online application, and the number is issued BY POST to the Irish address after the application completes. Neither gov.ie's service page nor Citizens Information publishes a guaranteed turnaround: there is no official service level for how long a PPSN takes.
rows.actual_reality: The ‘issued within 5 business days’ line this corridor previously carried was wrong and has been removed: no official Irish source states it, and it described the decision rather than the process. What governs the real elapsed time is appointment availability plus post. On the verified 2026-08-15 ES→IE case in Dublin the number took 10–20 business days (2–4 weeks) from arrival, and the employer withheld PAYE on the emergency basis for the whole of that period — see ie:payroll:ie-emergency-tax-before-ppsn. Two knock-on facts the official page does not connect: the clock cannot start on the day of arrival unless temporary accommodation is already booked, because the address proof comes from it (see ie:housing:ie-dublin-rental-payslip-reality); and the appointment, not the decision, is the queue to attack — book it in the week of arrival.
rows.action_required: Obtain a PPSN (Personal Public Service Number)
rows.source_name: Citizens Information — ‘Personal Public Service (PPS) number’: MyWelfare application, mandatory in-person appointment at a PPS Number Allocation Centre, proof of identity and of an Irish address, number issued by post; you cannot apply before you are in Ireland (page edited 5 August 2026)
rows.notes: Corrected 2026-08-17 to close gate rule no_wrong_requirements (wrong item 1, ‘PPS number issued within 5 business days’) from cvr:ES-IE:2026-08-15:andrea. The block edit reaches every corridor that references this block, which is the point of the split. Secondary source read 2026-08-17: gov.ie, ‘Get a Personal Public Service (PPS) Number’ (Department of Social Protection, last updated 30 January 2026), https://www.gov.ie/en/service/12e6de-get-a-personal-public-service-pps-number/ — it also publishes no processing time. The 10–20 business day figure is case-reported, not a service level. Not lawyer-verified.

rows.official_guidance: NON-OBVIOUS: without a Revenue Payroll Notification in place before the first pay run, PAYE is deducted at the emergency rate — the Irish analogue of the "tax card before first pay" trap.
rows.action_required: Register the employment with Revenue (myAccount / RPN)

rows.official_guidance: NON-OBVIOUS: proof of address is a chicken-and-egg barrier on arrival. Most movers bridge with a digital account until a traditional one can be opened.
rows.action_required: Open an Irish bank account

rows.official_guidance: NON-OBVIOUS: public healthcare eligibility hinges on an "ordinarily resident" test and GP visits are normally paid out of pocket, so a newcomer is effectively on private cover at first. Proof of cover is also needed for immigration registration.
rows.action_required: Arrange private health insurance and register with a GP

rows.official_guidance: If you keep your Norwegian employer while living and working in France, the default outcome is FRANCE, not Norway: a permanent relocation falls under the place-of-work rule — it is not a posting, so no A1 exemption applies. This determination drives the employer’s URSSAF obligation and your withholding setup. Verify against nav.no and the EEA coordination rules.
rows.action_required: Determine which social-security system applies (EEA Reg. 883/2004)

rows.official_guidance: Non-EEA nationals need a French long-stay visa or residence permit granted BEFORE establishing in France. This corridor draft covers the French/EEA-citizen return profile in depth — for a non-EEA move, have the immigration chain confirmed by a regulated professional before committing to dates.
rows.action_required: French long-stay visa / residence permit — route to an immigration professional

rows.official_guidance: Sequencing trap: deregistration from the Folkeregister can disable the BankID you will still need to file the exit-year Norwegian tax return from abroad. Confirm with your bank how to keep BankID working before the move notice takes effect.
rows.action_required: Preserve BankID before deregistering from Norway

rows.official_guidance: Close out the Norwegian tax card and confirm the final salary settlement around departure so the exit-year figures are clean. Source: skatteetaten.no.
rows.action_required: Cancel / settle the Norwegian tax card (skattekort) and final payroll

rows.official_guidance: Membership of the Norwegian scheme must end in step with the social-security determination — a gap leaves you uncovered, an overlap risks double contributions. Needs input from both you and the employer. Source: nav.no / folketrygdloven.
rows.action_required: End folketrygden (Norwegian National Insurance) membership

rows.official_guidance: Norwegian health cover ends with departure. The trap is the COVERAGE GAP between HELFO ending and French CPAM cover starting — plan the CPAM registration immediately so the gap is as short as possible. Source: helfo.no.
rows.action_required: End HELFO health cover and handle the EHIC

rows.official_guidance: Only applies if you receive Norwegian benefits — they must be notified of the move abroad around departure. Source: nav.no.
rows.action_required: Notify NAV of any active benefits (barnetrygd etc.)

rows.official_guidance: Wind down Norwegian contracts and set up mail forwarding — but keep ONE Norwegian bank account open until the exit-year tax refund has cleared.
rows.action_required: Close or transition Norwegian banking, insurance, lease, utilities and mail

rows.official_guidance: The legal move-abroad notice to the Norwegian population register, due within roughly 8 days around departure (verify the current rule at skatteetaten.no). If you have already left Norway and this window has elapsed, it renders red — file it retrospectively now.
rows.action_required: Report the move abroad to Folkeregisteret (flyttemelding via Skatteetaten)

rows.official_guidance: Gather proof of more than 12 months of Norwegian residence and more than 6 months of ownership of the goods you are bringing. This Phase A paperwork is exactly what unlocks the French transfer-of-residence customs relief later — without it the import relief claim stalls.
rows.action_required: Assemble Norway exit evidence for French customs relief

rows.official_guidance: Staying temporarily with family? The proof-of-address package is: attestation d’hébergement from the host + the host’s own proof of address + proof of relationship/ID. Nearly every French registration hangs off this — do it as early as possible. Source: service-public.fr.
rows.action_required: Establish a justificatif de domicile (proof of address) — attestation d’hébergement if hosted

rows.official_guidance: As a French citizen you have an unconditional right of entry and residence — no visa, permit, or immigration registration is required. Evaluated and confirmed: nothing to do here.
rows.action_required: Immigration / right to enter and reside in France

rows.official_guidance: France has no mandatory citizen address registry — there is no French equivalent of the Folkeregister to register with. Evaluated and confirmed: nothing to do here.
rows.action_required: Population / address registration in France

rows.official_guidance: Needed for salary, CPAM reimbursements and admin. French banks ask for the proof-of-address package first — have the justificatif de domicile ready.
rows.action_required: Open a French bank account

rows.official_guidance: Register with CPAM (via PUMA or as a worker; ask HELFO about an S1 handoff if applicable) within weeks of arrival. This closes the coverage gap left when HELFO cover ended — until CPAM confirms, you are between systems. Source: ameli.fr.
rows.action_required: Register with CPAM for French health cover (carte vitale)

rows.official_guidance: Norwegian tax residence ends per the exit rules and the exit-year skattemelding must still be filed — possibly with utflyttingsskatt (exit tax) on latent share gains. Spans departure through the following tax year. Source: skatteetaten.no/utflytting.
rows.action_required: Norwegian tax-residence cessation and exit-year return

rows.official_guidance: Once French legislation applies, the Norwegian employer must register with URSSAF (service firmes étrangères) — OR use the Art. 21, Reg. 987/2009 arrangement where the employee remits contributions on the employer’s behalf. The employer is almost certainly unaware this obligation exists. It is THEIR obligation — shown here so it is not orphaned. Source: urssaf.fr.
rows.action_required: Norwegian employer’s French social-contribution registration (URSSAF)

rows.official_guidance: An employee working from France can create a French taxable presence for the Norwegian employer. INFORMATION ONLY — this is the employer’s question for their own tax advisor under the FR–NO treaty; ReloPass does not issue this as advice.
rows.action_required: Permanent-establishment (PE) risk for the Norwegian employer

rows.official_guidance: Under Rome I, mandatory French employment provisions can apply to work physically performed in France even on a Norwegian contract. INFORMATION ONLY — route to a regulated professional for the specific contract.
rows.action_required: Governing labour law for work performed in France under a Norwegian contract

rows.official_guidance: Only if you bring a vehicle: customs clearance with possible VAT (waivable under the transfer-of-residence relief), the quitus fiscal, certificate of conformity (COC), then the carte grise via ANTS — within the French registration deadline after arrival (verify). Sources: douane.gouv.fr, ants.gouv.fr.
rows.action_required: Vehicle import from Norway (if you own a vehicle)

rows.official_guidance: Once the social-security and URSSAF questions are resolved, set up French income-tax withholding so pay is taxed correctly from the start. Source: impots.gouv.fr.
rows.action_required: Set up French withholding (prélèvement à la source)

rows.official_guidance: Folketrygd entitlements are preserved via the EEA coordination rules; private and occupational pensions are handled separately with each provider. No hard deadline — but confirm the paperwork rather than assume it. Source: nav.no.
rows.action_required: Preserve accrued Norwegian pension rights

rows.official_guidance: Declare your arrival to the French tax administration and obtain a numéro fiscal ahead of your first French declaration window. Source: impots.gouv.fr.
rows.action_required: French tax registration — declare arrival, obtain a numéro fiscal

rows.official_guidance: Norway is EEA but NOT the EU customs union — your household goods are a customs IMPORT into France, not free circulation. The relief requires proof of >12 months prior Norwegian residence and >6 months ownership, and is generally claimed within 12 months of establishing French residence (verify). The Norway exit paperwork is the evidence that unlocks it. Source: douane.gouv.fr.
rows.action_required: Household-goods import with transfer-of-residence relief (franchise de déménagement)

rows.official_guidance: French-resident income for work performed in France is taxable in France; the FR–NO treaty prevents double taxation in the split year. Handle it in your first French declaration cycle. Sources: FR–NO tax treaty, impots.gouv.fr.
rows.action_required: Income-tax split year and FR–NO treaty relief

rows.official_guidance: Dogs travelling to Norway from EU/EEA require: (1) ISO 11784/11785 microchip (implanted before rabies vaccination); (2) valid rabies vaccination with 21-day wait after primary (no wait for booster); (3) anti-echinococcus (tapeworm) treatment by authorised vet 24–120 hours before arrival, or alternative 28-day rule; (4) valid EU pet passport certified by authorised vet. No titre test required from EU/EEA. Exception: no tapeworm treatment needed if travelling directly from Finland, Malta, Ireland, or Northern Ireland. Maximum 5 pets for non-commercial movement. Six dog breeds are banned in Norway.
rows.actual_reality: Norway is EEA (not EU) but has adopted EU pet travel regulations (Regulation 576/2013 and 577/2013). EU pet passports are accepted. The 28-day tapeworm treatment rule allows frequent travellers to maintain regular treatment rather than treating 24–120 hours before every trip. Anti-echinococcus treatment must use praziquantel or equivalent. Banned breed imports are illegal — crossbreeds with banned breeds are also prohibited.
rows.action_required: Pet import into Norway — dog travelling from the EU/EEA

rows.official_guidance: Dogs entering France from another EU Member State or from Norway/EEA under the intra-EU rules require: (1) ISO 11784/11785 microchip (or legible pre-3-July-2011 tattoo) implanted BEFORE vaccination; (2) valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks or older, valid from 21 days after the first injection, boosters up to date; (3) a valid EU pet passport issued by an authorised veterinarian, with section 10 clinical examination completed; (4) minimum age 15 weeks and at least one adult tooth; (5) registration with I-CAD within 7 days of arrival via a French veterinarian (EUR 12). No rabies titration test, no tapeworm treatment, no import permit, no quarantine. Maximum 5 animals per traveller for non-commercial movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events, after checking with the DDPP). 1st-category attack dogs are banned outright.
rows.actual_reality: This is the rule set that applies to a Norway→France relocation: Norway is not treated as a third country for pet movements into the EU (EEA Joint Committee Decision No 66/2016; Regulation (EU) 2019/1293 recital 3), so the Norwegian EU-model pet passport is accepted and no titration test applies. The two steps movers most often miss are the mandatory I-CAD registration within 7 days of arrival and the fact that France’s own minimum entry age is 15 weeks even though the vaccine may be given at 12 weeks. Tapeworm treatment is an outbound-to-Norway requirement, not an inbound-to-France one.
rows.action_required: Pet import into France — dog travelling from Norway or the EU/EEA
rows.source_name: Service-Public.fr (DILA) — ‘Ramener un chien ou un chat de l’étranger : quelles sont les règles ?’, vérifié le 23 juillet 2026

rows.official_guidance: Cats entering France from another EU Member State or from Norway under the intra-EU rules require: (1) ISO microchip implanted before vaccination; (2) valid rabies vaccination (first injection at 12 weeks or older, valid after 21 days); (3) valid EU pet passport with section 10 completed; (4) minimum age 15 weeks; (5) I-CAD registration within 7 days of arrival (EUR 12). No titration test, no tapeworm treatment, no permit, no quarantine, maximum 5 animals per traveller for non-commercial movement.
rows.actual_reality: No breed restrictions apply to cats. The operative traps on this route are the 15-week minimum age and the 7-day I-CAD registration, which is easy to miss because nothing at the border prompts it.
rows.action_required: Pet import into France — cat travelling from Norway or the EU/EEA
rows.source_name: Service-Public.fr (DILA) — ‘Ramener un chien ou un chat de l’étranger’, vérifié le 23 juillet 2026

rows.official_guidance: Ireland has no state allocation of housing: a mover arranges accommodation privately, and two official requirements depend on an address already being in place on the day of arrival. First, a PPS number cannot be applied for from abroad — the mover must already be in Ireland — and the MyWelfare application requires proof of an Irish address no more than three months old: a household utility bill, an official letter or document, a bank statement, a property lease or tenancy agreement, or written confirmation of address from the accommodation provider (a hotel or hostel manager or a property owner is accepted). Second, a prospective tenant may be asked for a reference from a previous landlord, a reference from their employer, proof of income such as payslips or bank statements, photo ID and a PPSN. There is no obligation to hand any of it over, but Threshold states plainly that withholding it may result in not being offered the property. A landlord may only require the PPSN once the tenant is accepted, in order to register the tenancy with the RTB.
rows.actual_reality: Dublin's rental market cannot be entered from outside the country, so the sequencing matters more than the search. Daft.ie counted 1,187 homes available to rent in Dublin on 1 May 2026 — down 23% year on year and one of the lowest May totals on record — with Dublin market rents up 4.3% in Q1 2026 alone, matching the largest quarterly rise on record. In a market that tight the income evidence decides the tenancy, and on the verified 2026-08-15 ES→IE case the mover was asked for three or more months of IRISH payslips: documents a new arrival cannot possibly hold. Her words were “I had no idea I would need payslips I could not possibly have yet.” The consequence is a hard pre-departure gate: roughly 6–8 weeks of temporary or serviced accommodation has to be BOOKED BEFORE DEPARTURE, because it is also what supplies the proof of Irish address the PPS number application needs, and the permanent tenancy only becomes winnable once the first Irish payslips exist. This SUPERSEDES the earlier ES→IE guidance that a mover should “allow 4–8 weeks to secure accommodation”: 4–8 weeks is achievable only when it runs FROM a temporary Dublin base, never instead of one. On an employer-supported move the temporary-housing allowance in the relocation package is the thing to check first — on the 2026-08-15 case it was shorter than the time the tenancy actually took.
rows.action_required: Book temporary Dublin accommodation before departure — treat the permanent tenancy as a post-arrival project
rows.source_name: Threshold (national housing charity) — ‘Seeking private rented accommodation’: information a landlord or agent may request, including an employer reference and proof of income such as payslips or bank statements
rows.notes: Authored 2026-08-17 to close gate rule no_missed_requirements (missed item 1) and to correct wrong item 2 (‘Dublin accommodation: allow 4–8 weeks’) from cvr:ES-IE:2026-08-15:andrea. Secondary sources, each read on 2026-08-17: Citizens Information, ‘Personal Public Service (PPS) number’ (accepted proof-of-address documents; you cannot apply before you are in Ireland), https://www.citizensinformation.ie/en/social-welfare/irish-social-welfare-system/personal-public-service-number/ (page edited 5 August 2026); Daft.ie Rental Report Q1 2026 (Prof. Ronan Lyons, Trinity College Dublin), https://www.daft.ie/report. HONEST LIMIT: the ‘three or more months of Irish payslips’ figure is case-reported by the mover on 2026-08-15 (docs/case-verification-reports/2026-08-15-andrea-es-ie.md), not an official rule — no Irish instrument sets a number of payslips, and a landlord asking for extensive financial data from every applicant before selecting a preferred tenant is questionable under the Data Protection Commission’s guidance. Not lawyer-verified.

rows.official_guidance: Emergency Tax is Revenue's alternative basis of deduction, applied whenever an employer cannot obtain a Revenue Payroll Notification (RPN). Two different regimes exist and the difference is large. Where the employer does NOT have the employee's PPSN, ALL pay is taxed at the higher rate of 40% from the first weekly or monthly payroll run. Where the PPSN has been supplied but the employment is not yet registered with Revenue, a single person's rate band applies for the first four weeks (20% up to the band, 40% above it) and from week 5 the entire income is taxed at 40%. In both regimes the emergency rate of USC is a flat 8% in 2026 on all income. To avoid Emergency Tax the employer must hold the PPSN AND the job must be registered with Revenue, so that an RPN can be requested before the first pay day. Where Ireland is the employee's first employment in the State the employer cannot register it: the employee registers it themselves in Revenue myAccount under PAYE Services → ‘Add Job or Pension Details’.
rows.actual_reality: On an ES→IE move this window is not avoidable, only shortenable, and the corridor should say so instead of presenting the RPN as a task with a due date. The PPSN cannot be applied for until the mover is physically in Ireland with an Irish address to prove, so there is always a period of Irish employment with no PPSN on file — which is the 40%-on-everything regime, not the gentler four-week rate-band version most guidance describes. On the verified 2026-08-15 Dublin case the PPSN took 10–20 business days from arrival and the mover was on emergency deductions for the whole of it; this was the single fact she reacted to most strongly: “Nobody told me I would be taxed at 40% while waiting.” The over-deduction is refunded once the RPN is in place, but only through payroll or an end-of-year review, so in cash-flow terms it lands exactly in the month the rental deposit and the temporary accommodation are being paid for. Two things shorten it and both happen before payday: book the PPS appointment in the week of arrival, and give the employer the number the day it issues rather than waiting for the card or letter to be filed.
rows.action_required: Plan for emergency tax between the first pay run and the PPSN — and clear it the day the number issues
rows.source_name: Revenue.ie — ‘Emergency Tax rules’: higher rate of 40% on all pay where no PPSN has been given; single person’s rate band for weeks 1–4 where the PPSN was given but the job is unregistered, 40% from week 5; emergency USC 8% in 2026
rows.notes: Authored 2026-08-17 to close gate rule no_missed_requirements (missed item 2: the real PPS timeline and its emergency-tax consequence) from cvr:ES-IE:2026-08-15:andrea. The timing half of that item is carried by ie:tax_registration:ie-ppsn, which was corrected in the same import; this block carries the tax consequence, which is a distinct obligation with a distinct owner and a distinct source. Secondary source read 2026-08-17: Revenue.ie, ‘Emergency Tax’ overview, https://www.revenue.ie/en/jobs-and-pensions/emergency-tax/index.aspx. The 10–20 business day figure is case-reported (docs/case-verification-reports/2026-08-15-andrea-es-ie.md), not a published service level. Information only — an individual Irish/Spanish tax position needs a regulated adviser; not lawyer-verified.

rows.official_guidance: A dog entering Ireland from Spain travels under the EU non-commercial pet movement rules ONLY if it arrives with its owner, or with an authorised person carrying the owner's written permission where the owner's own journey is within 5 days. On that route the dog must: (1) be microchipped to ISO 11784/11785, with the chip implanted BEFORE the rabies vaccination; (2) hold a valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks or older by an authorised vet, valid from 21 days after the primary injection; (3) travel with a valid EU pet passport issued in an EU country (or an EU Animal Health Certificate where the owner is not an EU resident); and (4) be treated for the tapeworm Echinococcus multilocularis with a praziquantel-containing product by a vet no less than 24 hours and no more than 120 hours before the SCHEDULED ARRIVAL TIME in Ireland, recorded in the passport. Ireland is one of only five territories (with Finland, Malta, Norway and Northern Ireland) that is free of this tapeworm and enforces the treatment on intra-EU arrivals; a dog that has not been correctly treated may be refused entry or quarantined under official control, at the owner's cost. Compliance checks on EU arrivals do not have to be booked, but are carried out on a spot basis, so the original paperwork — not copies — must be on the traveller. If the dog does NOT arrive with the owner (or within the 5-day window), or more than five animals travel, the movement is UNACCOMPANIED or COMMERCIAL and leaves the pet-travel rules entirely: the premises of origin must be registered with the Spanish competent authority, a vet must clinically examine the dog within 48 hours of departure, the dog must travel with its passport AND an Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate raised on TRACES NT and signed by an official government vet in Spain, carriage must be by an approved Type 2 transporter, and the animal arrives through the airport cargo terminal where the Border Control Post must be able to accept the consignment — Dublin Airport BCP, +353 1 615 7650, BCP.DublinAirport@agriculture.gov.ie. The tapeworm window applies to this route as well.
rows.actual_reality: Pet relocation was absent from this corridor as a category, and the mover on the verified 2026-08-15 ES→IE case named the reason it hurts: “I assumed EU to EU meant the pet paperwork was already done.” Two facts break that assumption. First, Ireland's tapeworm-free status means an intra-EU dog movement still has a hard 24–120 hour veterinary window immediately before arrival — the one step that cannot be brought forward, rescheduled cheaply, or fixed at the border. Second, and the trap that actually catches relocations: on the Madrid–Dublin routes the dog usually CANNOT travel with its owner. Ryanair carries no animals on any flight except assistance dogs on certain routes. Aer Lingus does not accept pets in the cabin or as checked baggage: pets must be booked through a pet agent to travel in the hold as manifest cargo, animals presented at passenger check-in ‘will not be accepted under any circumstance’, and nothing can be carried at all on any leg operated by Aer Lingus Regional (Emerald Airlines). A dog shipped as cargo, or arriving more than 5 days apart from its owner, is an UNACCOMPANIED movement — so the case needs TRACES NT certification by an official Spanish vet, a registered premises of origin, a 48-hour clinical exam, an approved Type 2 transporter and a Border Control Post slot at the Dublin Airport cargo terminal. That is weeks of lead time and a different set of paperwork from the pet passport the owner already has, which is why this belongs on the timeline before travel rather than in a footnote. Order matters biologically too: microchip before vaccination, and no travel until 21 days after the primary rabies injection — get the order wrong and the clock restarts.

rows.official_guidance: A cat entering Ireland from Spain travels under the EU non-commercial pet movement rules ONLY if it arrives with its owner, or with an authorised person carrying the owner's written permission where the owner's own journey is within 5 days. On that route the cat must: (1) be microchipped with a chip readable by a device compatible with ISO standard 11785, implanted BEFORE the rabies vaccination — a chip that cannot be read on entry can mean quarantine under official control or refused entry; (2) hold a valid rabies vaccination given at 12 weeks or older by an authorised vet, valid only once the immunity stated on the vaccine datasheet has developed — at least 21 days after the primary injection (booster vaccinations with no break in coverage carry no waiting period); there are no exemptions, even for arrivals from areas declared rabies-free; and (3) travel with a valid EU pet passport — note that from 22 April 2026 an EU pet passport is only a valid travel document where the owner primarily resides in the EU (regardless of citizenship); otherwise an EU Animal Health Certificate is required. NO TAPEWORM TREATMENT APPLIES TO CATS: DAFM states the Echinococcus multilocularis (praziquantel) treatment requirement for dogs only, so the 24–120-hour pre-arrival veterinary window that governs the dog route does not exist on the cat route. Cats from EU countries may enter Ireland through any port or airport; compliance checks on EU arrivals are carried out free of charge on a spot basis rather than pre-booked, so the original paperwork — not copies — must be on the traveller, and a maximum of 5 pets may travel under the pet-travel rules. If the cat does NOT arrive with the owner (or within the 5-day window), if any change of ownership is involved, or if more than five animals travel, the movement is UNACCOMPANIED or COMMERCIAL and leaves the pet-travel rules entirely: the premises of origin must be registered with the Spanish competent authority, a vet must clinically examine the cat within 48 hours of departure, the cat must travel with its passport AND an Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate raised on TRACES NT and signed by an official government vet in Spain, carriage must be by an approved Type 2 transporter, a cat under 15 weeks old cannot be shipped to Ireland at all, and the animal arrives through the airport cargo terminal where the Border Control Post must be able to accept the consignment — Dublin Airport BCP, +353 1 615 7650, BCP.DublinAirport@agriculture.gov.ie.
rows.actual_reality: This block exists separately from ie:customs:pet-import-dog-eu because the rules genuinely differ, and copying the dog block would state a false requirement: Ireland's tapeworm treatment obligation applies to DOGS ONLY — a cat needs no praziquantel treatment and has no 24–120-hour pre-arrival veterinary window, which removes the one dog-route step that cannot be rescheduled. What the cat route DOES share with the dog route is the trap that actually catches relocations: on the Madrid–Dublin routes the cat usually cannot travel with its owner. Ryanair carries no animals on any flight except assistance dogs on certain routes, and Aer Lingus accepts no pets in the cabin or as checked baggage — pets must be booked through a pet agent as manifest cargo in the hold, animals presented at passenger check-in 'will not be accepted under any circumstance', and nothing can be carried on any leg operated by Aer Lingus Regional (Emerald Airlines). A cat shipped as cargo, or arriving more than 5 days apart from its owner, is an UNACCOMPANIED movement: registered premises of origin, a clinical exam within 48 hours of departure, an Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate raised on TRACES NT and signed by an official Spanish vet, an approved Type 2 transporter, and a Border Control Post slot at the Dublin Airport cargo terminal — weeks of lead time and a different set of paperwork from the pet passport the owner already has. Biology still sets the floor on timing even on the accompanied route: microchip before vaccination, vaccination at 12 weeks or older, no travel until at least 21 days after the primary rabies injection — get the order wrong and the clock restarts — and a cat under 15 weeks old cannot be shipped unaccompanied at all.
